papers.title: Developmental Cues and Stage‑Matched Niches for Engineering Engraftable Human HSCs.
papers.abstract: Generating functional haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from human pluripotent stem cells remains a major goal for both regenerative medicine and the study of early human blood development. Achieving this requires a clear understanding of how HSC identity is established during embryogenesis and how these developmental cues can be recreated in vitro. Recent work from Prof. Hanna Mikkola's group has defined transcriptional signatures and niche interactions that mark the emergence and maturation of human HSCs in vivo. Complementary studies from Professor Elizabeth Ng's team have developed human pluripotent stem cell-based systems that recapitulate key stages of this ontogeny, generating haemogenic endothelium and HSC‑like cells capable of long‑term multilineage engraftment. In this perspective, drawing on the recent ISEH NIC webinar presented by Profs. Mikkola and Ng, we integrate insights from both developmental and engineered systems to outline shared principles of human HSC formation and highlight opportunities to refine in vitro strategies for producing fully functional HSCs. Teaser Abstract What can human development teach us about building haematopoietic stem cells in the laboratory? Inspired by presentations from Profs. Mikkola and Ng at the 2025 ISEH NIC webinar, this perspective highlights the developmental and engineering principles that underpin human HSC formation and considers how these insights are advancing efforts to generate durable, engraftable HSCs for translational and regenerative applications.

papers.title: Sequence-Programmed Peptide Nanozyme Hydrogel with Microenvironment-Responsive Dual Catalytic Activity for Infected Wound Healing.
papers.abstract: Natural enzymes orchestrate complex biological processes through highly coordinated and multifunctional catalysis, yet their practical translation is limited by poor stability and environmental sensitivity. Here, we report a peptide-engineered nanozyme hydrogel that enables programmable, microenvironment-responsive catalytic switching in response to the wound microenvironment for active regulation of wound healing. Inspired by the catalytic motifs of natural hydrolases and oxidases, an amphiphilic peptide (C-GAVFFAHHGGEE) was rationally designed to coordinate Cuand self-assemble into a β-sheet-rich nanofibrous hydrogel. The resulting system exhibits pH-dependent catalytic switching, functioning as an oxidase (OXD)-like nanozyme under acidic conditions to generate bactericidal reactive oxygen species for localized antibacterial activity (K = 32.45 mM, vₘₐₓ = 0.61 µM s), while transitioning to hydrolases (HYD)-like activity under alkaline conditions to hydrolyze prodrugs and modulate inflammatory responses (K = 888.15 mM, vₘₐₓ = 3.55 mM s). Distinct from conventional nanozyme-based wound dressings that provide isolated or static functionalities, this system dynamically links catalytic activity with the evolving wound microenvironment, thereby enabling coordinated intervention in bacterial infection, redox imbalance, and inflammation. In vitro studies demonstrate high cytocompatibility and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. In a diabetic infected wound model, the hydrogel achieved almost complete wound closure within 12 days, accompanied by enhanced re-epithelialization, reduced inflammation, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis. This work establishes a strategy for integrating environment-responsive, dual enzyme-mimetic catalytic switching within a single peptide-based material, offering a programmable platform for actively modulating complex wound healing

papers.title: Abrogation of EMP1 Mitigates MASH-Associated Hepatic Fibrosis through Suppression of the JAK/STAT Signaling Axis.
papers.journal: Biochemistry and cell biology = Biochimie et biologie cellulaire
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by fibrogenesis, posing high risks for cirrhosis and cancer. Epithelial membrane protein 1 (EMP1) is a biomarker in fibrosis, but its role in MASH is unclear.EMP1 expression was assessed in MASH mouse models (MCD/HFD-induced) and human MASH specimens. The functional effects of EMP1 silencing and overexpression were evaluated in vivo, focusing on steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, the interaction between EMP1 and the JAK/STAT pathway was examined. EMP1 expression was significantly upregulated in both murine MASH models and human MASH liver tissues compared to healthy controls. Functionally, in vivo silencing of EMP1 markedly attenuated hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammatory infiltration, and fibrogenesis in mice fed MCD or HFD. Conversely, EMP1 overexpression exacerbated MASH progression, with a pronounced effect on fibrogenesis. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that EMP1 promotes the phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3 via its specific interaction with JAK2, whereas silencing EMP1 disrupts JAK2-mediated activation of downstream signal transducers. This inhibition of the JAK/STAT axis resulted in the suppression of hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, a key event in fibrogenesis. Our findings establish EMP1 as a critical pathogenic mediator in MASH-related fibrosis. By directly regulating the JAK2/STAT1/3 signaling axis in HSCs, EMP1 promotes fibrogenesis, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of MASH.

papers.title: An inductive content analysis of cultural responsiveness in United States psychologist predoctoral internship substance use clinical training.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnicity in substance abuse
papers.abstract: Findings persist concerning treatment disparities in substance use disorders (SUDs) across racial ethnic minoritized (REM) groups in the United States (US). Inadequate cultural responsiveness in health service psychologists (HSPs)' clinical training may be underlying these treatment disparities. The purpose of this study was to qualitatively explore HSPs' predoctoral internship training in SUDs and audit the extent of cultural responsiveness in training. Findings encompassed low frequencies of culturally responsive training opportunities. Lack of cultural responsiveness is indicative of a color-evasive approach to existing training. Our findings can close research-practice-training gaps by informing future training in applications of culturally responsive practices.

papers.title: Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer-Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials.
papers.abstract: Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer-drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency. Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54-9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modification and nanoparticle formation conditions contribute to curcumin incorporation. Spectroscopic analyses suggested reduced curcumin aggregation following encapsulation, which preserved its photoactivity and promoted reactive oxygen species generation under blue-light irradiation. papers.title: Boldine enhances hyperthermia-induced apoptosis in AGS gastric cancer cells in association with attenuation of the HSF1-HSP stress response.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer presents therapeutic challenges owing to treatment resistance and stress adaptation. This study investigated whether boldine enhances mild hyperthermia-induced cytotoxicity in AGS gastric cancer cells and evaluated its association with attenuation of the heat shock response involving heat shock proteins (HSPs) and heat shock factor 1 (HSF1). METHODS AND RESULTS: AGS cells were pretreated with boldine (1 h) and exposed to 37-43 °C (30 min). Combined treatment reduced viability, wound closure, and colony formation more than single treatments. The apoptotic fraction increased from 8.08% in untreated controls to 28.79% with boldine alone and 3.55% with hyperthermia alone, reaching 46.33% after cotreatment. Cotreatment altered cell cycle distribution (S and G2/M fractions), increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and enhanced MAPK phosphorylation. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) pretreatment reduced ROS levels and apoptotic cell fraction while partially restoring HSP27 expression. Boldine suppressed HSP expression-most notably HSP27-and attenuated HSF1 phosphorylation under hyperthermia. In NCI-N87 cells, confirmatory experiments showed higher apoptosis after cotreatment, whereas hyperthermia did not further reduce viability or alter HSP levels. CONCLUSIONS: Boldine enhances hyperthermia-induced apoptosis in AGS gastric cancer cells in association with attenuation of the HSF1-HSP stress response and ROS accumulation, supporting boldine as a potential thermosensitizing adjunct in gastric cancer therapy.

papers.title: An AGC kinase cascade regulates ROP signaling for the correct timing of pollen germination.
papers.abstract: In flowering plants, the timing of pollen germination is crucial for successful fertilization and an important trait for seed and fruit crops. Environmental factors tightly regulate pollen germination, with germination-suppressing conditions on the pollen-producing anther and germination-promoting conditions on the receiving stigma. Using genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods, we show that this environmental sensitivity of pollen germination in Arabidopsis thaliana is regulated by a 3-PHOSPHOINOSITIDE-DEPENDENT KINASE 1 (PDK1)-AGC1.5/AGC1.7 kinase cascade. We show that PDK1 hyperphosphorylates downstream AGC1.5/7 kinases to enhance their activity. Pollen-specific phosphoproteomics identified multiple proteins involved in pollen growth whose phosphorylation is controlled by AGC1.5/7. Two germination-promoting RHO OF PLANTS GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTORS (ROPGEFs) are phosphorylated by AGC1.5/7 at a novel site, reducing ROPGEF plasma membrane polarization. Loss of PDK1-AGC kinase signaling resulted in precocious pollen germination on the anther, which was rescued by high AGC1.5 kinase activity. Conversely, AGC1.5/7 overexpression or a phosphomimic ROPGEF version inhibited precocious pollen germination. Distinct subcellular localization of PDK1 and AGC1 kinases upon pollen germination is likely to alleviate their inhibitory effect. Our data indicate that the correct timing of pollen germination requires the fine-tuned activity of a PDK1-AGC1 kinase cascade inhibiting ROPGEFs on the anther, preventing precocious pollen germination.

papers.title: ROR2-expressing acute myelogenous leukemia cells can be selectively targeted by anti-ROR2 CAR T cells.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have revolutionized the treatment of B-cell malignancies but have not yet succeeded in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), largely due to the lack of cell surface antigens that can distinguish leukemia cells from essential normal hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Here, we used a newly developed high-affinity monoclonal antibody (mAb) B16, which is specific for the surface ROR2 in both human and mouse. Although ROR2 is a developmentally restricted protein that is primarily expressed during embryogenesis, we find that ROR2 protein is generally expressed by AML cells, including leukemia stem cells (LSCs), in patients with adverse-risk disease. Consistently, ROR2 is undetectable in most normal postnatal tissues and HSCs. Additionally, ROR2 can activate STAT3 signaling in response to Wnt11 in AML. Employing the binding domain of the anti-ROR2 mAb, we generated anti-ROR2 CAR T cells that selectively eliminated ROR2-positive AML cells of these patients while sparing normal HSCs. Intravenous infusion of such anti-ROR2 CAR T cells into immune-deficient mice selectively eradicated engrafted ROR2-positive human AML cells, including LSCs, without adversely affecting non-neoplastic normal mouse tissues or hematopoiesis. We propose that anti-ROR2 CAR T cells may offer therapeutic benefit for AML patients.

papers.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms by which hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) maintain long-term (LT) hematopoietic capacity and transition from quiescence remain incompletely understood, limiting their in vitro expansion and applications. Accumulating evidence underscores the importance of maintaining a low protein synthesis rate for HSC function, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ribosome-associated proteins specifically enriched in HSCs and multipotent progenitors (MPPs) and found that RNA-binding protein gene with multiple splicing (Rbpms) is required for sustaining low protein synthesis rates in HSCs. Rbpms forms biomolecular condensates that sequester translation elongation factors and protein-folding chaperones from ribosomes, slowing translation elongation and ensuring proper protein folding in HSCs. Rbpms deletion led to accelerated protein synthesis, accumulation of misfolded proteins in HSCs, impaired LT hematopoietic reconstitution capacity, accompanied by aberrant exit from quiescence. Our findings unveil a unique mechanism of translation elongation regulation in HSCs and highlight significance of spatial compartmentalization and translational control in HSCs.

papers.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) spheroid model exhibits a characteristic extracellular matrix-rich fibrous capsule hindering drug penetration.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), or primary liver cancer, is one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. Liver cirrhosis, characterized by deposition of excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) secreted by hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), is the major risk factor of HCC development. Although anti-fibrotic therapies hold great promise in the treatment of HCC, conventional non-animal models lack the complexity of the tumor microenvironment, especially its ECM component, driving efforts to develop more representative platforms. In this context, we bioengineered HCC spheroids by co-culturing human HCC cells (HepG2) with human HSCs (LX-2) in different ratios using a soft-embossed microwell array platform. HCC spheroids, depending on their exact composition, displayed typical HCC features, such as the presence of an ECM-rich capsule, as revealed by immunostaining of collagen type I on intact spheroids after tissue clearing. We hypothesized that the presence of this capsule, which is involved in several stages of tumor progression, could act as a 'protective barrier' that regulates the penetration and delivery of therapeutic agents. This hypothesis was confirmed using our bioengineered HCC spheroids, in which the combined presence of HSCs and ECM hinders the penetration and therapeutic efficacy of a model chemotherapeutics (doxorubicin). This could be improved by concomitant enzymatic degradation of the ECM-rich capsule. Altogether, we propose our HCC model as a relevant platform to study tumor-tumor microenvironment interactions, gain mechanistic insights into HCC, identify novel therapeutic targets and evaluate (combination) therapies targeting tumor-tumor microenvironment while integrating ECM degradation with the (targeted) delivery of therapeutic agents.

papers.title: Specific effects of Pulsed Field Ablation on the cardiac tissue, the nervous system and the conduction system in experimental and clinical studies.
papers.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
papers.abstract: AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel ablation modality for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias and has rapidly reshaped contemporary electrophysiology practice. This article provides a comprehensive analysis on the mechanisms underlying the specific effects of PFA on myocardial, neural tissue structures, and the cardiac conduction system, integrating biophysical principles with preclinical and clinical evidence relevant to contemporary electrophysiology practice. METHODS AND RESULTS: This document provides an exhaustive mechanistic explanation for the preferential effects of PFA on myocardium and the limits of the 'tissue-selectivity' concept. The complex interplay between cellular and tissue-level biophysics, biological responses, and tissue regenerative capacity that determines differential susceptibility to electroporation across tissues is analysed. Distinct patterns of lesion formation and maturation following PFA are also reviewed, highlighting the temporal and histopathological differences compared with radiofrequency ablation. Additionally, lesion formation in heterogeneous substrates is analysed, including fibrotic and adipose-rich myocardium, where local electric field distribution critically influences lesion durability. CONCLUSION: The article further examines the interaction between pulsed electric fields and neural tissue, with emphasis on the phrenic nerve and intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system. While nerve stimulation and transient reversible conduction disturbances produced by reversible electroporation can occur during ablation, permanent neural injury appears extremely rare in current clinical experience. Finally, this manuscript examines current understanding regarding the specific effects of PFA on the cardiac conduction system, which according to the limited available evidence appear strongly dependent on electric field dose and anatomical proximity.

papers.title: Antifibrotic activity of Schistosoma japonicum-derived sja-miR-2a-3p in carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Liver fibrosis is a common consequence of chronic liver injury and is driven largely by persistent activation of hepatic stellate cells and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. We previously identified Schistosoma japonicum-derived sja-miR-2a-3p as a parasite-derived microRNA with antifibrotic activity in schistosomiasis-associated liver fibrosis. Whether this cross-species regulatory molecule also modulates fibrogenesis beyond the context of schistosome infection remains unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: We investigated the effects of sja-miR-2a-3p in a carbon tetrachloride-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis. Mice received systemic administration of sja-miR-2a-3p agomir during CCL₄-induced fibrogenesis, followed by assessment of histological liver injury, fibrosis, inflammation, HSC activation, HSC-associated apoptotic activity, and transcriptomic alterations. sja-miR-2a-3p agomir administration increased sja-miR-2a-3p abundance in serum and liver tissues and markedly attenuated CCL₄-induced hepatic injury and fibrosis, as evidenced by reduced liver weight index, Ishak fibrosis scores, collagen deposition, and hepatic hydroxyproline content. sja-miR-2a-3p treatment also suppressed HSC activation and extracellular matrix production, with decreased expression of α-SMA, Col1α1, Col3α1, and TGF-β. Moreover, enhanced cleaved caspase-3 signals were observed in desmin-positive HSCs, consistent with increased apoptotic activity in activated HSCs. Hepatic expression of the inflammatory mediators TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 was also reduced. Whole-liver transcriptomic analysis further showed treatment-associated downregulation of extracellular matrix-, cytokine-, chemokine-, NF-κB-, IL-17-, and TNF-related pathways. papers.title: CHK1/2 as a potential therapeutic target in Neurofibromatosis type 2 schwannomas.
papers.abstract: The Merlin protein, encoded by the tumor suppressor gene Neurofibromatosis type II (NF2), serves as a linker between the actin cytoskeleton, the plasma membrane receptors, and other intracellular signaling molecules. While there is a basic understanding of how Merlin regulates oncogenic signaling pathways, current targeted therapies have yet to demonstrate consistent clinical efficacy. Using a library of protein kinase inhibitors, we found that NF2-null Schwann cells (SCs) were uniquely sensitive to prexasertib, a drug that targets the DNA damage response pathway kinases CHK1/2 (Checkpoint Kinase 1 and 2). NF2-null SC proliferation was also sensitive to small molecule inhibitors of CHK1/2 downstream effectors. At baseline, NF2-null SCs have increased RAC1 activity, elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and higher levels of DNA damage. Exposing NF2-null SCs to DNA damaging agents such as doxorubicin or carboplatin, alone or in combination with prexasertib, further decreased their proliferation. Consistent with this idea, suppressing RAC1 or NOX2 activity with small molecule inhibitors, decreased ROS production and restored resistance to prexasertib in NF2-null hSCs, suggesting that active RAC1 and high ROS render NF2-null hSC uniquely vulnerable to DNA damage. Furthermore, restoring NF2 expression in NF2-null Schwann cells restored their resistance to prexasertib, reduced RAC1 activity, and lowered levels of ROS and DNA damage. The intrinsic elevation of RAC1, ROS, and DNA damage in NF2-null hSCs suggest that inhibiting DNA damage response pathways might be clinically useful in patients with NF2-null schwannomas.

papers.title: Transient ATM inhibition enhances knock-in efficiency in hematopoietic stem cells by attenuating the DNA damage response.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Precise genome editing in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) holds great potential for treating inherited blood disorders; however, low knock-in (KI) efficiency and loss of functional HSCs after genome editing remain major obstacles. Here, we demonstrate that transient inhibition of Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated (ATM) kinase markedly enhanced KI efficiency in mouse HSCs genome-edited with Cas9/ribonucleoprotein (RNP) and AAV donor DNA. Phosphoproteomic and capillary western blot analyses revealed that ATM inhibition suppressed aberrant Cas9-AAV-induced ATM activation and the subsequent DNA damage response, reduced p53-dependent apoptosis, and enhanced survival of KI HSCs. In serial transplantation assays, ATM inhibition preserved long-term engrafting KI HSCs, increasing their frequency from ~0.3 to 40% in secondary recipients, an over 100-fold improvement. Furthermore, in an X-linked severe combined immunodeficient mouse model, ATM inhibition increased KI efficiency and restored T- and B cell differentiation. Comprehensive safety analyses, including long-read nanopore sequencing, amplicon deep sequencing, whole genome sequencing and clonal tracking, did not detect increased genomic alterations, chromosomal abnormalities, or clonal expansion following transient ATM inhibition. Taken together, these findings establish transient ATM inhibition as an effective strategy to enhance KI-mediated genome editing while maintaining the long-term repopulating capacity of HSCs.

papers.title: Pan-cancer analysis reveals DNAJC9 as an immune-related biomarker and a positive regulator of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: : Heat shock proteins (HSPs) modulate apoptosis, proliferation, and differentiation, positioning them as potential therapeutic targets in cancer. As a member of the J-domain-containing HSP40 family, DnaJ homolog, subfamily C, member 9 (DNAJC9) has not yet been systematically investigated in a pan-cancer context.: Multiple public repositories were employed to perform a comprehensive pan-cancer investigation of DNAJC9. We also utilized single-cell datasets to explore how DNAJC9 expression varies across distinct cellular clusters. These efforts covered several key dimensions, including diagnostic and prognostic value, immune landscape, genomic alterations, methylation differences, and pathway enrichment. To determine its biological effects, DNAJC9 was silenced in lung cancer cell lines, and subsequent experiments assessed cellular phenotypes. The downstream PI3K/AKT signaling cascade was examinedwestern blotting.: Across multiple tumor types, DNAJC9 was markedly upregulated, especially in advanced-stage cases, and higher expression levels predicted worse prognosis. DNAJC9 expression also correlated significantly with immune infiltration, tumor mutation burden (TMB), and microsatellite instability (MSI). Tumor tissues showed substantially lower DNAJC9 methylation than normal tissues. Single-cell analysis detected DNAJC9 expression in multiple immune cell subsets. Knockdown of DNAJC9 in A549 and H1299 lung cancer cells impaired proliferation, migration, and invasion. Functional enrichment analysis then pointed to the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Western blotting further confirmed that silencing DNAJC9 reversed the activated PI3K/AKT cascade in these cells, as shown by decreased p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios.: Pan-cancer analyses suggest that DNAJC9 may serve as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker across cancers. papers.title: A new reporter strategy reveals a subset of nonmigratory hematopoietic stem cells located in a dynamic bone marrow niche.
papers.abstract: Interactions of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) with the bone marrow microenvironment are critical to regulate stem cell function in homeostasis, emergency hematopoiesis and ageing. The dynamic behavior of endogenous HSCs in their niches has been challenging to study due to the complexity of markers required to define pure HSCs. Multiple recently developed reporter strategies advanced our capacity to identify HSCs in situ. Yet, they provide different levels of HSC enrichment and are frequently not stable in situations of perturbed hematopoiesis, leading to contradictory observations of HSC localization and migratory behavior. Here we employed a new double reporter strategy by combining the Hoxb5-mKO2 and Vwf-GFP reporters, that are stably expressed in homeostasis, stress and ageing. Hoxb5+Vwf+ cells represent a subset of highly pure and potent long-term HSCs with a platelet-biased pattern of differentiation, that are included in the populations identified by other reporter strategies. Intravital microscopy revealed Hoxb5+Vwf+ cells to be non-migratory in homeostasis, ageing, or following acute thrombocytopenia when these cells are actively proliferating, indicating that this non-migratory behavior is independent of cell cycle status. We found Hoxb5+Vwf+ HSCs in perivascular niches with a higher coverage by LepR+ mesenchymal cells but not preferentially located closer to megakaryocytes, when compared to Hoxb5+Vwf- cells. Nevertheless, stress-induced megakaryopoiesis following acute thrombocytopenia bring megakaryocytes into closer proximity of Hoxb5+Vwf+ HSCs, revealing previously unrecognized niche dynamics in HSC regulation during regeneration.

papers.title: Context-dependent protective and pathogenic functions of YTHDF1 in MASLD and hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms and design of therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and can progressively develop into inflammatory metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis. During this progression, activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) leads to excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix. There is a growing trend to develop into hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The limited availability of effective therapeutics highlights the need to better understand the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a key post-transcriptional RNA modification that regulates gene expression and governs a broad range of physiological and pathological processes. YTH domain family 1 (YTHDF1) is a reader protein that recognizes m6A modifications on mRNAs and enhances their stability or translation by interacting with key components of the translation machinery. YTHDF1 exhibits context-dependent functions in MASLD and liver fibrosis, while it promotes HCC pathogenesis. Hepatocytic YTHDF1 alleviates MASLD by improving mitochondrial function, serving as a protective factor during its early stages. YTHDF1 in HSCs is important for initiating liver fibrosis, yet it also plays a crucial role in regulating HSC ferroptosis to counteract established fibrosis. Our structure-based analyses of YTHDF1 inhibitors reveal novel concepts, including inhibition of YTHDF1-induced condensates and direct degradation of YTHDF1 proteins by fullerene derivatives and metal-organic frameworks. YTHDF1 inhibitors serve as selective chemical probes for interrogating YTHDF1's cell type-specific functions in MASLD. They are also promising candidates for in vivo evaluation to treat MASLD and HCC and to prevent liver fibrosis at early stages.

papers.title: Efficient Generation of Definitive-like Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells through Optimized Lateral Plate Mesoderm Induction and a Supportive Endothelial-Stromal Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The generation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) with definitive features from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) requires coordinated lineage specification together with a supportive hematopoietic microenvironment. Although 3D and aggregate-based systems can recapitulate endothelial and stromal niche features, their self-organizing architecture can introduce structural heterogeneity and batch-to-batch variability, complicating experimental standardization and process control. Here, we developed a chemically defined, feeder-free, lateral plate mesoderm (LPM)-directed 2D multicellular system that combines controlled hematopoietic specification with the spontaneous formation of an endothelial-stromal microenvironment. Through sequential differentiation from LPM to hemogenic endothelium, this system generated CD34CD43CD45HSPCs at frequencies of up to 86% across three hPSC lines within 10 days. Notably, an endothelial-stromal microenvironment formed spontaneously without aggregate formation, and disruption experiments implicated Notch and CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling in hematopoietic progenitor development. Transcriptomic benchmarking revealed HSC-associated molecular features in the generated cells while also identifying residual transcriptional differences from primary cord blood LT-HSCs. The resulting HSPCs exhibited clonogenic activity and multilineage differentiation potential, giving rise to enucleated erythrocytes, cytotoxic natural killer cells, and phenotypically identified monocyte-like and T-lineage cells, with erythroid enucleation reaching approximately 80%. In addition, day-10 suspension-derived CD34cells showed detectable bone marrow engraftment in vivo. Collectively, this study shows that key microenvironmental features can be retained within a simplified 2D multicellular system, providing a framework for studying hematopoiesis and refining hPSC-derived HSPC generation. papers.title: Epigallocatechin gallate and thermal cycling‑stimulation synergistically promote apoptosis in A549 cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress‑induced calcium ion dysregulation and oxidative stress.
papers.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as the predominant subtype of lung cancer, presents a considerable clinical challenge due to its high rates of recurrence and the significant adverse effects associated with conventional therapeutic modalities. In response to these challenges, the present study has explored the combined anticancer effects of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) together with thermal cycling‑stimulation (TCS). The findings obtained demonstrated that the combination of EGCG and TCS led to a synergistic decrease in the viability of A549 and NCI‑H460 NSCLC cells, whereas IMR‑90 normal lung fibroblasts exhibited minimal cytotoxic effects. Further investigations revealed that EGCG could mitigate the TCS‑induced upregulation of the heat shock proteins (HSPs) HSP70 and HSP105, whereas the expression levels of proteasome subunits were concurrently decreased. These alterations were accompanied by the disruption of proteostasis, and also by the activation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‑associated pathways. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition studies suggested a mutual interplay between inositol 1,4,5‑trisphosphate receptor‑mediated ER Ca2+ release and an excessive production of reactive oxygen species, ultimately causing the cells to undergo mitochondrial apoptosis. In summary, the present study has shown that the combined treatment of EGCG and TCS reduces the required dosage of EGCG, while also attenuating TCS‑induced heat shock responses. Consequently, the present study offers a novel and promisingproof‑of‑concept strategy for treating NSCLC.

papers.title: Redox-metabolic cascade NIR-II prodrug for synchronizing compensatory HSPs/P-gp feedback with mitophagy flux impairment against intrinsic thermotolerance.
papers.abstract: The intrinsic proteostasis of HSPs/P-gp remains formidable barriers in the multidrug resistance (MDR) and thermotolerance. To dismantle the compensatory HSPs and P-gp defense axis, we developed a metabolic reprogramming NIR-II nanoprodrug Lipid 2-DG@Au/DOX-ss, using gold liposome-nanorod loaded disulfide-doxorubicin prodrug DOX-ss and 2-deoxy-d-glucose (2-DG). Results revealed 2-DG dose-dependent metabolic perturbations of ATP, glucose, NAD, LDH. Coupled with a 24.01-fold ROS enhancement, a 5.05-fold PINK1 surge, a 0.65-fold LC3-II accumulation, 0.29-fold p62 increase, S-phase arrest (up to 64%), intensive mitophagy flux impairment was initiated to terminal cell death via NF-κB/PINK1/LC3-II pathway. Proteomic analysis further elucidates the concurrent inhibition of HSP70 (A12A)/90/B1(27)-mediated protein folding with P-gp efflux pump downregulation and the disruption of mitochondrial autophagic clearance, as well as unveiling the potent in immune modulation, ferroptosis, and calcium homeostasis. This bioenergetics-derived nanoprodrug with HSPs/P-gp compensation and mitophagy impairment provides a precise approach for eradicating recalcitrant MDR malignancies.

papers.title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model. LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples. CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

papers.title: Stopping, opening, and redirecting fluid flow in paper-based microfluidic devices using thermo-responsive gelatin valves.
papers.abstract: The advancement of microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (µPADs) toward complex biochemical assays is hindered by the lack of reliable, low-cost fluid-control strategies capable of providing defined sealing and actuation times. The environmental sensitivity of passive barriers depends on their material composition and formulation, whereas many active valves require comparatively complex fabrication. This work introduces a thermo-responsive gelatin valve as a simple, inexpensive, and biocompatible approach to fluid control. Valve performance was optimized by varying gelatin concentration, cooling conditions, storage duration, and actuation temperature. A concentration of 30 mg mLprovided the most suitable balance between closed-state retention and thermal responsiveness. Porometry and contact-angle measurements indicated that the gelatin-treated region reduced accessible capillary pathways and exhibited a water contact angle of approximately 99°, thereby preventing flow at room temperature. Under controlled heating at 40 °C, the optimized valve opened in approximately 20 s. The valve was integrated into a paper-based acetylcholinesterase inhibition assay for malathion. A single-shot design reduced the number of liquid-addition steps by combining sample delivery and incubation in one operation. The calculated limit of detection (LOD) was 0.24 µM, below the drinking-water guideline value of approximately 0.88 µM. A 0.5 µM malathion spike in St. Lawrence River water produced a recovery of 86.1 ± 3.2%. The device is presented as a proof-of-concept screening platform, with further matrix validation required before regulatory drinking-water analysis. These findings establish gelatin as a tunable material for timed fluid control in paper microfluidic devices.

papers.title: Environmental sensitivity and perceived social support in relation to adolescent eating disorder symptoms.
papers.abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) frequently emerge during adolescence and are influenced by both individual and contextual factors. Among these, perceived social support has generally been associated with better outcomes, although findings remain inconsistent and may depend on both the source of support and individual differences in responsiveness to environmental inputs. The present study examined the role of Environmental Sensitivity (ES) and perceived social support in adolescent ED symptoms, focusing on different sources of support and their potential interaction within a vantage sensitivity framework. A sample of 466 adolescents (51.61% female; M = 14.80) completed self-report measures of ED symptoms, ES, and perceived social support. At a bivariate level, higher perceived support from family, teachers, friends, and peers was associated with lower ED symptoms. In covariate-adjusted models, only teachers' and family's support remained a significant predictor, while peer-related sources were no longer associated with ED symptoms. ES was consistently and positively associated with ED symptoms. Contrary to hypotheses, ES did not moderate the association between overall perceived social support and ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses suggested a sex-specific pattern, whereby the association between perceived social support and ED symptoms appeared to vary as a function of ES among males, but not females. These findings suggest that the association between social support and adolescent ED symptoms may depend on its source. Moreover, ES was consistently associated with ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses revealed that evidence for differential responsiveness to supportive contexts may vary by ES among males.

title.#text: Targeting activated hepatic stellate cells through ferroptosis: phenethyl isothiocyanate attenuates CCl-induced liver fibrosis by regulating iron metabolism, redox homeostasis, and autophagy.

papers.abstract: Phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC), a dietary compound from cruciferous vegetables, is known for its chemopreventive activity, but its effects on liver fibrosis remain largely unexplored. In this study, we show that PEITC administration attenuated carbon tetrachloride (CCl)-induced hepatic injury and fibrosis in mice, as evidenced by reduced collagen deposition, hydroxyproline content and fibrotic marker expression, and improved liver function. PEITC inhibited cell survival and fibrogenic phenotypes in transforming growth factor β (TGF-β)-stimulated LX-2 human hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) while exhibiting minimal cytotoxicity towards normal hepatocytes. Mechanistically, PEITC depleted glutathione, inhibited glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid peroxidation, and malondialdehyde, thereby triggering ferroptosis, as also confirmed by transmission electron microscopy showing mitochondrial shrinkage, increased membrane density, and cristae loss. Additionally, PEITC activated autophagy and promoted nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4)-mediated ferritinophagy, leading to ferritin degradation. The involvement of autophagy was further validated by co-treatment with autophagy inhibitors, which partially reversed PEITC-induced ferritin heavy chain (FTH1) downregulation and NCOA4 upregulationimmunofluorescence staining revealed that PEITC suppressed antioxidant defense and promoted ferritin degradation in activated HSCs, as shown by reduced GPX4 and FTH1 fluorescence signals within α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive areas in mouse liver sections. Collectively, these findings elucidate that PEITC alleviates liver fibrosis by promoting ferroptosis-related processes in activated HSCs, mainly through the NCOA4/FTH1 axis, positioning it as a promising nutraceutical candidate for antifibrotic therapy.

papers.title: Elevated asymmetric dimethylarginine drives hematopoietic stem cell metabolic reprogramming and dysfunction in chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is commonly linked to hematopoietic abnormalities beyond the well-recognized anemia, with underlying mechanisms poorly understood. Here, we show that asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA), which accumulates in the CKD microenvironment, perturbs hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis. Clinical data analysis reveals that serum ADMA levels rise with CKD progression and inversely correlate with the myeloid-to-lymphoid ratio. Notably, ADMA compromises HSC quiescence and long-term repopulating capacity, as observed in CKD mouse models established by 5/6 nephrectomy. Further investigations demonstrate that ADMA hyperactivates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, promoting the transition from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation and inducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction in HSCs. Mechanistically, ADMA binds with high affinity to protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit Bβ (PPP2R2B), relieving its inhibition of mTOR signaling. Inhibition of mTOR signaling by rapamycin or clearance of ROS by N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) reverses ADMA-induced HSC functional defects. Collectively, our findings identify ADMA as a key mediator of CKD-associated hematopoietic dysfunction via the PPP2R2B-mTOR-mitochondria axis, providing a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Adult hematopoietic stem cells activate a normally fetal-restricted program to functionally expand ex vivo.
papers.abstract: The ability to robustly expand transplantable hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) ex vivo enables basic science and clinical therapies otherwise hindered by the scarcity of these self-renewing multipotent cells. Despite recent improvements in long-term ex vivo HSC expansion conditions, the molecular mechanisms required for successful ex vivo expansion of functional HSCs remain unknown. Here we characterized the ex vivo expansion potential of HSCs from mouse fetal liver, young bone marrow, and aged bone marrow at the functional and molecular levels. We find that Lin28b, the in vivo fetal-restricted gene, contributes to the mechanism of both fetal and adult ex vivo HSC expansion. The expression of Lin28b correlates with reconstitution potential, with higher levels observed in HSCs expanded from the fetal liver and young adults. By contrast, expanded aged HSCs fail to robustly express Lin28b and also fail to stably reconstitute the hematopoietic system following transplantation. Consistent with a functional role for this fetal program in ex vivo expanded HSCs, Lin28b-deficient HSCs display aging-associated molecular and functional features following ex vivo expansion cultures. Importantly, Lin28b overexpression during ex vivo expansion was sufficient to enhance reconstitution potential of aged HSCs. In summary, we identify Lin28b as an important regulator of functional HSC expansion ex vivo, suggesting novel opportunities for HSC rejuvenation and clinical applications.

papers.title: Parental support moderates the interaction of COMT and BDNF genotypes with early life adversity on problem gambling severity index scores among young adults.
papers.abstract: The development of gambling-related harm and gambling disorder involves several genetic and environmental factors. However, how these factors interact to influence the development and whether such interactions confer to diathesis-stress or differential susceptibility models remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, data from the Survey of Adolescent Life in Västmanland (SALVe cohort) were utilized, Participants provided a saliva sample for genotyping, completed early life adversity (ELA) and Parents as Social Construct (PASCQ) surveys at age 17, and the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) at age 23. A total of 391 participants (54% females) with complete data were included for analysis. Negative binomial models were utilized to examine the interaction between candidate genes (COMT, BDNF, and DRD2), ELA, and parental support in PGSI scores. Interactions between COMT and BDNF, ELA, and parental support were found but not for DRD2, (β = -0.01 and -0.009, 95% CI [-0.02, -0.006 and -0.01, -0.005], p = 2.2 × 10and 1.2 × 10respectively). The interactions remained significant after accounting for sex interactions, p = 0.005. Notably, evidence for a differential susceptibility framework was found in gambling-related harm scores. Participants with the major allele for both COMT and BDNF displayed plasticity by exhibiting higher PGSI scores when exposed to weak parental support but lower PGSI scores in strong parental support despite higher ELA scores. Positive parental support acted as a protective factor against the genetic sensitivity of gambling-related harm. Studies pursuing the interplay between genetic and environmental factors would benefit from including positive environments that may mitigate the risk associated with adverse environments.

papers.title: Identification of the HSP gene family in wild Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus) and analysis of their expression during different hibernation stages.
papers.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
papers.abstract: Hibernation is an extreme form of seasonal heterothermy that enables animals to survive under harsh environmental conditions and provides valuable natural models for investigating the physiological mechanisms underlying stress tolerance. The Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus) is a small burrowing mammal that exhibits pronounced seasonal changes in activity and naturally undergoes hibernation, making it a useful model for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying hibernation. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are highly conserved molecular chaperones involved in protein homeostasis and cellular stress responses. A total of 40 HSP genes were identified in the Daurian ground squirrel and grouped into six subfamilies, consisting of three small HSPs (sHSPs), 26 HSP40s, six HSP70s, three HSP90s, one HSP60, and one HSP110. Comprehensive analyses of molecular characteristics, conserved domains, gene structures, phylogenetic relationships, and chromosomal distributions revealed substantial evolutionary diversity within the HSP40 family. Although members of the DNAJA, DNAJB, and DNAJC subfamilies shared several conserved structural features, differences were also observed in their molecular characteristics and evolutionary relationships. To investigate their expression dynamics during hibernation, the transcript levels of HSP40 genes in the liver tissues of the Daurian ground squirrels at different hibernation stages were quantified using the real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Most of the HSP40 genes examined exhibited broadly similar expression trends throughout the hibernation cycle, although individual genes showed different temporal expression profiles. These findings suggest that HSP40 genes undergo differential transcriptional regulation during hibernation and may be involved in the physiological responses associated with hepatic adaptation to the hibernation state. Collectively, this study provides a systematic characterization of t

papers.title: Targeting RPL4 improves the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Activation and progressive accumulation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are pivotal events in the progression of liver fibrosis, and no effective treatments are available to date. Hepatic FBXL6 promotes hepatocarcinogenesis, but the function of FBXL6 in tissue stromal cells remains unknown. Here, FBXL6 is highly expressed in the activated HSCs in human fibrotic livers. HSC-specific FBXL6 overexpression or deletion is achieved by crossbreeding Fbxl6or Fbxl6mice with Pdgfrβ-Cre mice. FBXL6 drives liver fibrosis in mice, whereas FBXL6 deletion attenuates chemical- or MASH-induced liver fibrosis. Mechanistically, FBXL6 promotes the polyubiquitination and activation of a previously uncharacterized substrate, RPL4, which requires JNK2-mediated phosphorylation at Ser295. Activated RPL4 upregulates YY1, increases PD-L1, and then activates the AKT/mTOR pathway, leading to extracellular matrix production and liver fibrosis. Furthermore, the knockdown of RPL4 enhances the efficacy of anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in FBXL6-driven liver fibrosis in mice, which provides a promising therapeutic strategy for liver fibrosis treatment.

papers.title: Biliverdin reductase A deficiency reveals sex- and brain region-specific vulnerability to high-fat diet feeding.
papers.abstract: How the brain senses and responds to early metabolic stress, and why this process fails differently across sexes and regions, remains poorly understood. Here we show that biliverdin reductase A (BVRA) loss is associated with sex- and brain region-specific effects in response to high-fat diet (HFD) feeding, impairing insulin signaling and mitochondrial responses in selected brain regions while being associated with adaptive liver remodeling and improved systemic glucose handling in female mice. Using wild-type and whole-body BVRA-deficient mice of both sexes exposed to short-term high-fat diet (HFD) followed by dietary normalization, we show that BVRA loss is sufficient to induce cortical insulin resistance within just one week, phenocopying eight weeks of HFD and preceding detectable oxidative distress or mitochondrial failure. This sequence supports a model in which dysfunctional insulin signaling may represent an early event in the cascade of brain metabolic injury. The frontal cortex is the earliest and most vulnerable brain region, whereas the hippocampus shows delayed and milder alterations, suggesting brain region-specific vulnerability to HFD. Strikingly, F mice develop cognitive impairments indistinguishable from M mice despite substantially milder molecular alterations, revealing a sex-specific dissociation between molecular severity and functional outcome. After dietary normalization, M mice show partial recovery of cortical insulin signaling, mitochondrial function, and recognition memory. In contrast, F mice exhibit progressive BVRA decline, worsening insulin signaling uncoupling, and persistent cognitive deficits that outlast dietary exposure - revealing a metabolic memory encoded at the molecular level. These findings identify BVRA loss as a potential causal and sex-biased determinant of brain metabolic vulnerability, with implications for understanding the sex-differential susceptibility to insulin resistance-related neurodegeneration.

title.#text: Differential Susceptibility and HR-Like Resistance Responses intoand.

papers.abstract: Hemibiotrophic fungi of the genusprovide valuable systems for studying plant immunity and pathogen lifestyle transitions; however, compatible and incompatible interactions have rarely been compared within the same host species. Here, we show thatexhibits contrasting responses to two phylogenetically distinct hemibiotrophic fungi,KACC40803 andKC05. Multilocus phylogenetic analyses using,,, andsequences confirmed their taxonomic identities. The two fungi also differed morphologically, particularly in colony characteristics and appressorial structures. Inoculation ofleaves withcaused progressive chlorosis, necrotic lesions, extensive fungal colonization, acervulus formation, and increasing fungal biomass, indicating a compatible susceptible interaction. Host defense-related genes associated with salicylic acid- and jasmonic acid-mediated pathways were suppressed during infection. By contrast,.induced restricted lesion development, rapid accumulation of callose and reactive oxygen species, localized plasma membrane disruption, and strong induction of defense-related genes inleaves, consistent with an incompatible hypersensitive response (HR)-like cell death. Fungal biomass remained low throughout infection, demonstrating effective restriction of colonization. Together, these findings establish a dual-pathosystem that enables comparative analysis of susceptibility and HR-like resistance within a single host, providing a tractable model for dissecting host specificity, immune signaling, and regulated cell death during hemibiotrophic infection. title.#text: Age-related IGF-1 decline permits a redox-sensitive transcriptional shift that directs hematopoiesis toward a CCR2myeloid fate.

papers.abstract: Aging reshapes hematopoiesis toward myelopoiesis, particularly increased output of classical monocytes, contributing to immunosenescence. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify that aging drives hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to progressively commit to a CCR2monocyte fate along a defined lineage trajectory, which is executed through a redox-sensitive transcriptional cascade. We find that the age-related decline in bone marrow IGF-1 is the upstream niche signal that releases suppression of the oxidative stress/NF-κB/IRF8 axis, allowing this cascade to redirect early progenitors toward a CCR2myeloid-primed fate. Functional assays confirm that cells following this CCR2trajectory drive myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and directly contribute to age-associated immunosuppression. Our work delineates a hierarchical pathway from niche decay to lineage redirection, establishing the CCR2fate trajectory as a key driver of immunosenescence and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Enhancing the Functionality of Human Bone Marrow-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Using Signaling Modulators.
papers.abstract: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (BM-MSCs) possess an inherent capacity to support hematopoiesis in vitro. As a result, they are often used as feeder layers for the ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) or coinfused with HSCs to improve the success of clinical transplants. However, MSCs isolated from non-hematopoietic tissues such as adipose or dental tissue may not be as effective as BM-MSCs in supporting hematopoiesis. Additionally, BM-MSCs tend to lose their functional ability after extended in vitro culture, which is necessary for producing sufficient cell numbers for clinical use. These limitations underscore the importance of pretreating MSCs with suitable signaling modulators to boost their functionality. Reliable in vitro assays play a crucial role in finding such signaling compounds and evaluating their effects on MSCs. Conventional assays, such as long-term-culture-initiating assay (LTC-IC assay) or colony-forming-unit assay (CFU assay), chemotactic migration assays (e.g., Transwell assay), etc., primarily evaluate the functional competence of HSCs and HSPCs, but provide little insight into the hematopoiesis-supportive capacity of MSCs. This chapter describes two such assays: one is designed to assess the hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC)-supporting capacity of primed MSCs, and the other is specifically aimed at their ability to support the growth of primitive HSCs. These assays can serve as initial screens to test the impact, whether positive or negative, synergistic or antagonistic, of known signaling compounds, bioactive peptides, growth factors, and cytokines on MSC function or to discover new entities that could boost the functionality of MSCs.

papers.title: Using patient iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium to evaluate differential susceptibility to MEK inhibitor-associated retinopathy.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Compare the effect of MEK inhibition on iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells generated from a patient who developed MEK inhibitor-Associated Retinopathy (MEKAR) versus a patient who did not develop retinopathy. This is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating comparison of one donor line per clinical phenotype. DESIGN: Exploratory case-control comparison (one patient-derived line per phenotype) SUBJECTS: Two female patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 who were treated with MEK inhibitors. One patient developed MEKAR, the other did not. METHODS: RPE were generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) from these two patients. These hiPSC-derived RPE were treated with selumetinib for 10 days. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Phagocytic activity and changes in gene expression. RESULTS: As previously reported, there was a significant increase in internalized rhodopsin in phagocytosis assays, yet this was only found in hiPSC-derived RPE from the patient who developed MEKAR. Selumetinib decreased expression of genes related to fluid transport and cell volume, including aquaporins and solute transporters. At baseline, cells from the patients without MEKAR had higher expression of these genes. Interestingly, selumetinib-induced changes in gene expression only reached statistical significance in cells from the patient who did not develop MEKAR, suggesting these changes may be a compensatory protective mechanism. Patients susceptible to forming MEKAR may have increased phagocytosis without a compensatory change in expression of genes related to fluid flux, thereby inhibiting their ability to transport fluid out of the subretinal space. Because only one donor line was studied per clinical phenotype, and because the two donors also differ in age, NF1 variant class, and MEK inhibitor exposure, these associations are hypothesis-generating and cannot be attributed to MEKAR status independently of donor background. papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals atorvastatin modulates the tumor microenvironment to suppress breast cancer liver metastatic outgrowth.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains incurable, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological and preclinical evidence suggests statins suppress metastatic outgrowth, however the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We employed high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) to explore the cellular composition and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the metastatic microenvironment following atorvastatin treatment. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded breast cancer liver metastases from control and atorvastatin-treated mice were analyzed by Nanostring CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI)/Bruker using a 973-gene panel, profiling 212 and 207 tumor-adjacent field of views (FOVs) (TAFs) respectively, which identified eight cell clusters, while non-tumor FOVs (NTFs) were sparse. Preferential depletion of LRRC15⁺ myofibroblastic cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs), CXCL8⁺ inflammatory CAFs, and C1QC⁺/SPP1⁺ tumor associated macrophages (TAMs) subsets were revealed by harmony-assisted cell annotation and Seurat label transfer, which further separated CAFs and TAMs into discrete functional subpopulations. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was also performed to validate cell types in both the tissues. Wilcoxon-based DEG analysis identified metastasis-associated gene expression changes between groups. Atorvastatin treatment reduced CAFs, Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) (significantly), and macrophages (trending) in TAFs, with no changes in NTFs. These findings were supported by IHC (n = 4), which confirmed prominent reductions in these cell types while hepatocyte and endothelial markers remained unchanged. DEG analysis revealed coordinated downregulation of metastasis and extracellular matrix- associated transcripts in atorvastatin-treated TAFs. papers.title: HIF-1α-ASS1 axis drives reprogramming of arginine metabolism controls hepatic stellate cell activation in hepatic fibrosis.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.abstract: Dysregulated arginine metabolism promotes hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and liver fibrosis. However, the mechanisms underlying arginine hosmeostasis in hepatic fibrogenesis and therapeutic targeting remain unclear. Using Multicellular hepatic spheroid (MCHS) models recapitulating in vivo liver fibrosis, we investigated the effects of arginine deprivation or supplementation. Genetic and pharmacological (ABRL8301, a 2-methoxyestradiol derivative) inhibition of hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha (HIF-1α) were assessed for effects on argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) expression and antifibrotic efficacy in vitro and in vivo. Holotomography and quantitative imaging approaches characterized cellular and molecular fibrogenic changes. Arginine deprivation increased MCHS compactness and α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression, whereas l-arginine supplementation reversed effects. Considering pivotal roles of ASS1 and arginase 1 (Arg1) in arginine biosynthesis and catabolism, respectively, ASS1 overexpression suppressed mesenchymal markers, whereas Arg1 overexpression aggravated fibrotic signatures. HIF-1α knockdown and ABRL8301 treatment upregulated ASS1, reduced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and fibrotic markers, and enhanced arginine biosynthesis in MCHSs. Holotomography analysis confirmed ABRL8301 attenuated TGFβ1-induced cell elongation and α-SMA fiber accumulation in HSCs and fibroblasts. In CCl₄-mouse liver fibrosis models, ABRL8301 significantly reduced collagen deposition, necrosis, and fibrosis. Combination sorafenib and ABRL8301 therapy decreased MCHS compactness, increased apoptosis, and achieved superior tumor control in HCC xenografts. Restoring arginine metabolic homeostasis through HIF-1α inhibition-mediated ASS1 upregulation suppresses HSC activation and liver fibrosis.
